conditions.name: Pregnancy
conditions.intakeQuestion: Are you pregnant? If so, how many weeks?

flags.why: Take 400 mcg folic acid daily until 12 weeks. A higher dose (5 mg) is prescribed if you have diabetes, take epilepsy or HIV medicines, or have a family history of neural tube defects.
Take 10 mcg (400 IU) a day from October to March, or all year if you rarely get sun on your skin or have dark skin. Do not take more than 100 mcg a day.
Do not take vitamin A (retinol) supplements, cod liver oil or liver products. Too much can harm the baby.
Iron is checked with blood tests during pregnancy. Take iron if your midwife or doctor advises it.
US thyroid experts advise a 150 mcg iodine supplement a day for people planning pregnancy, pregnant or breastfeeding. Seaweed products vary a lot in iodine.
Needs rise in pregnancy and most prenatal vitamins contain little or none.

flags.nutrient: caffeine (including fitness supplements and energy drinks)
flags.why: Keep caffeine under 200 mg a day. Some fitness supplements contain caffeine.
Not all natural remedies are safe in pregnancy. Check with your pharmacist, midwife or GP first.
It may increase the risk of birth defects.
Should not be used in pregnancy. It is linked to harm in newborns.
Experts advise avoiding it in pregnancy.
May cause early labour or extra bleeding at delivery.
Turmeric supplements may be unsafe in pregnancy.
Not safe in pregnancy in more than food amounts; linked to birth defects.
Large amounts are linked to early delivery.
Not recommended in pregnancy because safety is not known.
B6 can ease pregnancy sickness, but ask first. Long-term very high doses can damage nerves; the adult upper limit is 100 mg a day.

habits.title: Aim for 150 minutes of moderate activity a week, including 2 strength sessions
habits.why: Exercise is safe in pregnancy and can lower the risk of gestational diabetes and pre-eclampsia.

habits.title: Avoid alcohol
habits.why: There is no known safe level of alcohol in pregnancy.

habits.title: Try ginger for mild sickness
habits.why: Guidelines suggest ginger for mild to moderate pregnancy sickness if you prefer not to take medicine.

habits.title: Eat no more than 2 portions of oily fish a week
habits.why: Oily fish can contain pollutants, such as mercury, that can harm your baby in large amounts.

doctorQuestions: Do I need the higher 5 mg dose of folic acid?
Should I take iron, iodine or a pregnancy multivitamin?
Are my regular medicines and supplements safe in pregnancy?
Is my vitamin D intake enough?

conditions.name: Breastfeeding
conditions.intakeQuestion: Are you breastfeeding at the moment?

flags.why: Consider 10 mcg (400 IU) vitamin D a day in autumn and winter.
US thyroid experts advise a 150 mcg iodine supplement a day while breastfeeding.
Breastfed babies of mothers who eat no animal foods may have very low B12 reserves. Make sure you get enough B12.
The product information says to avoid it while breastfeeding, as there is no data on breast milk.
Should not be used while breastfeeding; it can harm newborns.
Should not be used while breastfeeding.
Breastfed babies of mothers taking it can have colic, drowsiness and lack of energy.
Not recommended because safety while breastfeeding is not known.
High caffeine intake can make breastfed babies fussy and sleep poorly.
Little is known about whether ginkgo is safe while breastfeeding.
Needs are higher while breastfeeding (550 mg a day).

habits.title: Eat at least 2 portions of fish a week, but no more than 2 portions of oily fish
habits.why: Fish is good for you and your baby.

habits.title: Eat plenty of fibre and drink plenty of fluids
habits.why: Fibre can help with bowel problems and constipation after birth.

doctorQuestions: Are my supplements and medicines safe while breastfeeding?
Do I need iodine, vitamin D or B12?
If I eat a vegan diet, what does my baby need?

conditions.name: Trying to get pregnant
conditions.intakeQuestion: Are you trying to get pregnant, or could you become pregnant in the next few months?

flags.why: Take 400 mcg folic acid daily, ideally from 3 months before pregnancy. Some people need a higher 5 mg prescription dose.
Avoid high-dose vitamin A (above 3,000 mcg or 10,000 IU a day) if you could become pregnant; too much can cause birth defects.
National advice is not to take herbal remedies if you are trying to get pregnant.
Consider 10 mcg (400 IU) vitamin D a day, at least in autumn and winter.

habits.title: Start folic acid at least a month before trying to conceive
habits.why: US experts advise 400 to 800 mcg folic acid a day for anyone who could become pregnant, starting at least 1 month before conception.

doctorQuestions: Do I need the higher 5 mg dose of folic acid?
Are my medicines and supplements safe if I become pregnant?

conditions.name: Type 1 diabetes
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you have type 1 diabetes and use insulin?

flags.why: It may increase the effect of insulin and raise the risk of low blood sugar.
It can lower blood sugar and may add to the effect of insulin.
Large doses may cause a harmful drop in blood sugar.
Type 1 diabetes is listed as a common risk factor for low B12. Ask if a test makes sense for you.

habits.title: If you drink alcohol, check your sugar afterwards
habits.why: Alcohol can cause a delayed low when you use insulin.

doctorQuestions: Could any of my supplements change how much insulin I need?
Should I be tested for coeliac disease?
Should my B12 level be checked?

conditions.name: Type 2 diabetes
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you been told you have type 2 diabetes? Which diabetes medicines do you take, for example metformin, insulin or a tablet that makes your body release more insulin?

flags.why: Metformin can lower B12 over time. Ask about a blood test now and then, especially with tingling feet, tiredness or anaemia.
It can lower blood sugar. With diabetes medicines it may push sugar too low, and it changes how some medicines are handled.
It may add to the sugar-lowering effect of diabetes medicines and cause lows. Any benefit is small and unclear.
Benefit for blood sugar is unclear. Using cinnamon supplements with diabetes medicines can cause unwanted side effects, and large amounts of cassia cinnamon may worsen liver disease.
Using aloe with diabetes medicines can cause unwanted side effects.
Diabetes can lower magnesium, but supplements are not advised just to lower blood sugar. Keep supplements to 350 mg a day or less unless your doctor says otherwise.
Trials show little effect on blood sugar in diabetes. Do not go above 4,000 IU (100 mcg) a day unless your doctor advises it.
High-dose niacin can raise blood sugar. The upper limit from supplements is 35 mg a day.
Large doses may cause a harmful drop in blood sugar.
It might lower blood sugar. Check with your doctor first if you have diabetes.
In a study it lowered metformin levels by about a quarter, which could weaken sugar control.
Psyllium fibre taken before meals lowered fasting sugar and HbA1c in trials of people with type 2 diabetes. If you use insulin or sugar-lowering tablets, watch for lows.

habits.title: Walk for about 10 minutes after each main meal
habits.why: In a trial this lowered sugar after meals more than one daily 30-minute walk, most after the evening meal.

habits.title: Break up long sitting with short, light walks
habits.why: In short lab trials, light walking breaks lowered sugar and insulin after meals compared with sitting still.

habits.title: Do structured exercise: brisk activity, strength work or both
habits.why: Structured exercise lowered HbA1c in many trials; more than 150 minutes a week worked better.

habits.title: Eat more high-fibre foods (at least 14 g fibre per 1,000 calories)
habits.why: Diabetes guidelines advise high-fibre, minimally processed carbohydrate foods.

habits.title: If you drink alcohol, check your sugar afterwards
habits.why: Alcohol can cause a delayed low, especially with insulin or tablets that boost insulin.

doctorQuestions: I take metformin. Should my vitamin B12 be checked, and how often?
Could any of my supplements make my blood sugar go too low with my diabetes medicines?
Is my kidney function healthy enough for the supplements I take?
Do I need to change anything about my medicines on days I exercise or drink alcohol?
What should my blood sugar be after meals?

conditions.name: Prediabetes (blood sugar higher than normal)
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you been told your blood sugar is higher than normal but not yet diabetes, sometimes called prediabetes or borderline diabetes?

flags.why: In 3 trials of people with prediabetes pooled together, vitamin D lowered the chance of getting diabetes by about 15%. Ask your doctor if it suits you.
US diabetes guidelines do not advise vitamin D for everyone with prediabetes. They note that giving it to millions of people could raise the risk of side effects.
If you take metformin long term, ask about B12 checks, especially if you have anaemia or nerve symptoms.
It may lower blood sugar, but studies are limited and it can change how other medicines work.
Any benefit for blood sugar is small and unclear. Rare cases of liver and kidney problems have been reported.
It is unclear if it helps. Cassia cinnamon contains coumarin, and long-term use may be a problem for people with liver disease.
It may slightly improve how your body uses insulin. Keep supplements to 350 mg a day or less unless your doctor says otherwise.
Psyllium fibre gave a modest drop in blood sugar in people at risk of diabetes.

habits.title: If you are overweight, aim to lose about 7% of your body weight
habits.why: In a large trial, a lifestyle programme cut new diabetes by more than half, and worked better than metformin.

habits.title: Be active for at least 150 minutes a week, like brisk walking
habits.why: This was a core part of the lifestyle programme that prevented diabetes in trials.

habits.title: Take short, light walks during long periods of sitting
habits.why: In short lab trials, light walking breaks lowered sugar and insulin after meals compared with sitting.

doctorQuestions: Is my risk high enough to talk about metformin or vitamin D?
How often should my blood sugar (HbA1c) be rechecked?
Is there a diabetes prevention or lifestyle programme I can join?
If I start metformin, should my B12 be checked?

conditions.name: Kidney disease (reduced kidney function)
conditions.intakeQuestion: Has a doctor told you that your kidneys are not working fully, for example chronic kidney disease, or that you need dialysis or have a kidney transplant?

flags.why: Weak kidneys may not clear potassium, so even normal amounts can build up. Avoid potassium supplements and potassium salt substitutes unless your kidney team agrees.
Magnesium can build up to harmful levels when the kidneys are weak.
Kidney disease can upset the balance of minerals in bones and blood. Ask your health care team before using vitamin or mineral supplements.
Kidney experts list creatine as high risk for people with kidney disease.
Some people with kidney disease need moderate protein so waste does not build up, but too little can cause poor nutrition. Ask a dietitian how much is right.
High intakes may raise oxalate in urine and could add to kidney stones, especially in people with kidney problems.
People with kidney disease may be more sensitive to harm from high chromium intakes.
Even small amounts have been linked to severe side effects, such as heart rhythm problems, in people with kidney conditions.
These are not proven and some ingredients can harm the kidneys or interact with medicines.

flags.nutrient: green or 'superfood' powders, seaweed and electrolyte products
flags.why: These can be high in potassium or phosphorus.
Kidney experts list it as high risk because it interacts with many other medicines.
In anaemia caused by kidney disease, iron is guided by regular blood tests from your kidney team.

habits.title: Ask for advice on potassium, phosphate, salt and calories for your stage
habits.why: Guidelines advise diet advice matched to how severe the kidney disease is.

habits.title: Exercise, keep a healthy weight and do not smoke
habits.why: Advised for adults with kidney disease in national guidance.

habits.title: Cut down on processed foods with added phosphate
habits.why: Added phosphate in processed foods raises blood phosphorus more than natural sources.

habits.title: Use herbs and spices instead of salt substitutes
habits.why: Many salt substitutes are high in potassium.

doctorQuestions: What stage is my kidney disease, and how much protein, potassium and phosphate should I have?
Which of my vitamins or supplements are safe for my kidneys?
Should I take a prescribed form of vitamin D or calcium?
Do I need a referral to a kidney dietitian?

conditions.name: Kidney stones
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you ever had kidney stones?

flags.why: High doses raise oxalate in urine, which may add to kidney stones.
One large study linked calcium supplements to more kidney stones, but later reviews did not. Keep calcium in your diet and ask your doctor about supplements.
Too much vitamin D can raise calcium and cause kidney stones. Stay within 4,000 IU (100 mcg) a day unless your doctor advises more.
Turmeric supplements may raise the risk of kidney stones. Ask first if stones run in your family.

habits.title: Drink 2.5 to 3 litres of water a day, unless your doctor has told you to limit fluids
habits.why: Pale urine is a sign you are drinking enough.

habits.title: Keep salt under 6 g a day, get enough calcium in your diet, and limit fizzy, caffeinated and alcoholic drinks
habits.why: Advised to help prevent kidney stones.

doctorQuestions: What type of stone did I have, and does it change what I should eat or drink?
Are my calcium, vitamin C and vitamin D supplements safe for me?
How much fluid should I drink each day?

conditions.name: Liver disease
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you been told you have a liver condition, such as fatty liver, hepatitis or cirrhosis?

flags.why: Liver damage has been reported in some people taking high-absorption curcumin products.
A few reports link ashwagandha to liver problems.
Liver injury has been reported, mostly with green tea extract tablets or capsules.
Kava has been linked to rare but serious liver injury.
Rare cases of liver damage, some very serious, have been reported with products labelled as black cohosh.
Long-term use of cassia cinnamon, which contains coumarin, could be a problem for people with liver disease.
People with long-term liver disease clear manganese poorly and are more likely to be harmed by high intakes.
High doses of niacin taken for months or years can damage the liver.

habits.title: Stop a supplement and see a doctor if you get dark urine, yellow skin or eyes, tiredness, nausea or poor appetite
habits.why: These can be signs of liver damage.

doctorQuestions: Which supplements are safe for my liver?
How much alcohol, if any, is safe for me?
Should my liver blood tests be checked before I start a new supplement?

conditions.name: Heart disease
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you have a heart condition, such as angina, a past heart attack, heart failure or an irregular heartbeat?

flags.why: Some heart and blood pressure medicines raise potassium. Do not take potassium supplements or potassium salt substitutes unless your doctor agrees.
In two large trials, 4 g a day of omega-3 for several years slightly raised the risk of an irregular heartbeat (atrial fibrillation) in people with or at high risk of heart disease.
Licorice can cause irregular heartbeat and even cardiac arrest. Even small amounts are linked to severe effects in people with heart conditions.
Some reviews linked calcium supplements to heart disease, but other studies found no link.
Vitamin E supplements were linked to more bleeding strokes in two trials.
It can weaken some heart medicines, such as digoxin and ivabradine.
Furosemide can lower thiamin (vitamin B1), and low thiamin is common in heart failure.

habits.title: Do aerobic and muscle-strengthening activity at a level that is safe for you
habits.why: Advised for people with or at high risk of heart disease.

habits.title: Swap saturated fats for olive or rapeseed oil
habits.why: Advised for people at high risk of or with heart disease.

doctorQuestions: Which supplements are safe with my heart medicines?
Should my potassium or kidney function be checked?
How much exercise is safe for me, and should I join a rehab programme?

conditions.name: High blood pressure
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you been told you have high blood pressure? Do you take medicine for it?

flags.why: Not advised for older people, people with diabetes or kidney disease, pregnant women, or people on ACE inhibitors or ARBs.
Calcium, magnesium and potassium supplements are not advised as a way to lower blood pressure.
Even small amounts have been linked to severe side effects in people with high blood pressure.
Too much coffee and other caffeine-rich products is discouraged for people with high blood pressure.
Side effects of green tea extract supplements include increased blood pressure.

habits.title: Keep salt low
habits.why: Less salt can lower blood pressure.

habits.title: Eat a healthy diet and exercise regularly
habits.why: Both can lower blood pressure.

habits.title: Cut down on alcohol if you drink a lot
habits.why: This can lower blood pressure and has other health benefits.

doctorQuestions: What should my blood pressure be?
Are my supplements or salt substitute safe with my blood pressure medicines?
Should my kidney function and potassium be checked?

conditions.name: High cholesterol
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you been told you have high cholesterol? Do you take a statin or another cholesterol medicine?

flags.why: Some products contain a statin-like drug in unknown amounts, with the same possible side effects and interactions as statins.
Not advised as a way to prevent heart disease.
Added to statins in large trials, high-dose niacin did not cut heart events, and one trial found more strokes.
UK guidance says there is no evidence that omega-3 products help prevent heart disease, except one prescription form.

habits.title: Keep saturated fat low and use olive or rapeseed oil
habits.why: Advised for people at high risk of heart disease.

habits.title: Do aerobic and muscle-strengthening activity
habits.why: Advised for people at high risk of heart disease.

doctorQuestions: What is my overall heart risk, and do I need a statin?
Are my supplements safe with my cholesterol medicine?
When should my cholesterol be rechecked?

conditions.name: Varicose veins or long-term vein problems in the legs
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you have varicose veins, or legs that often feel heavy, achy or swollen, with skin changes or sores around the ankles?

flags.why: In short-term trials, horse chestnut seed extract eased leg pain and swelling. Larger trials are still needed.

flags.nutrient: horse chestnut (raw seeds, bark, flowers or leaves)
flags.why: These parts are unsafe to take by mouth. Only standardised seed extract has been used safely in studies, for up to 12 weeks.

See a doctor first if you have skin inflammation, a hard or painful vein, severe pain, ulcers, sudden swelling of one or both legs, or heart or kidney failure. Not recommended in pregnancy or breastfeeding.
In placebo-controlled trials it eased leg pain, heaviness, cramps and swelling.
Common side effects are stomach upsets such as diarrhoea and nausea. Avoid while breastfeeding.
As a group, they ease swelling a little but do not clearly improve quality of life, and they slightly increase side effects.

habits.title: Exercise regularly, for example walking
habits.why: A European vein guideline advises exercise to reduce vein symptoms.

habits.title: Do exercises that strengthen your calf muscles
habits.why: In a small trial in people with severe vein disease, 6 months of calf exercise improved calf pump function and strength, though symptom scores did not change.

habits.title: Try compression stockings for aching or swelling, if a professional says they suit you
habits.why: A European vein guideline recommends stockings of at least 15 mmHg at the ankle to ease symptoms.

habits.title: Ask whether vein treatment would suit you better than stockings
habits.why: UK guidance offers stockings mainly when vein treatment is not suitable.

habits.title: Ask a professional to check stockings are safe for you
habits.why: Stockings are usually safe when used correctly and after checking for reasons not to use them. Skin irritation, discomfort and pain are the most common problems; serious harm is very rare.

habits.title: Raise your legs when resting and avoid standing or sitting still for long periods
habits.why: Symptoms are often worse after standing and better with your legs up.

habits.title: Keep to a healthy weight and do not smoke
habits.why: Advised for varicose veins; smoking damages your veins.

habits.title: Know when to get help
habits.why: See a GP for painful, itchy or swollen legs or a sore that has not healed after 2 weeks. Get urgent help if a vein bleeds.

doctorQuestions: Do I need a scan or a referral to a vein specialist?
Are compression stockings safe for me, and which pressure and length should I use?
Is a vein supplement safe with my other medicines?
What signs mean I should get help quickly, such as a painful, red or swollen leg?

conditions.name: Taking a blood thinner
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you take a medicine to thin your blood or prevent clots, such as warfarin, apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, edoxaban, aspirin or clopidogrel?

flags.why: On warfarin, sudden changes in vitamin K from food or supplements can change how warfarin works. Keep intake steady and ask before any product with vitamin K.
It can weaken warfarin and many other important medicines.
Large doses of vitamin E with blood thinners can increase the risk of bleeding.
May increase bleeding risk with blood thinners such as warfarin.
Garlic supplements may increase bleeding.
Turmeric may increase bleeding with blood thinners.
High-dose fish oil can affect platelets. On warfarin, your INR may need checking.
CoQ10 may interact with warfarin.
Ginseng may interfere with blood clotting.
Some horse chestnut products may increase bleeding with blood thinners.

habits.title: Eat steady amounts of vitamin K foods, like leafy greens, from week to week
habits.why: On warfarin, avoid sudden large changes in these foods.

habits.title: Tell your clinic before you start or stop any supplement
habits.why: Many supplements change bleeding risk or how blood thinners work.

doctorQuestions: Which supplements are safe with my blood thinner?
If I take warfarin, how much vitamin K food is OK and when should my INR be checked?
What signs of bleeding should make me get help?

conditions.name: Surgery or a procedure coming up
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you have an operation or procedure planned, including dental surgery? Roughly when?

flags.why: Tell your team about every supplement. Anaesthetists may ask you to stop supplements at least 2 weeks before.
Garlic supplements may increase bleeding. Tell your team, especially before surgery.
Linked to bleeding. Stop before surgery as your team advises.
Linked to bleeding and low blood sugar.
It speeds up how the body breaks down many medicines used around surgery.
Kava can increase the effect of anaesthesia.
Ask how to taper it in the weeks before surgery. Do not stop suddenly after long use.
Guidance based on a 2021 expert consensus says to hold vitamin E for 2 weeks because of a theoretical bleeding risk.
Guidance based on a 2021 expert consensus says to hold turmeric for 2 weeks because of a theoretical bleeding risk.
Some professionals advise stopping fish oil, but a large heart-surgery trial found it did not increase bleeding. Follow your team's advice.
Experts do not recommend it for people about to have surgery.
If you have iron-deficiency anaemia, guidelines advise iron tablets before and after surgery.

habits.title: Bring all your supplement bottles to your pre-surgery check
habits.why: Many people forget to mention supplements. Seeing the bottles helps the team plan safely.

habits.title: Ask what you can eat and drink before the operation
habits.why: Guidelines allow clear drinks up to 2 hours and food up to 6 hours before anaesthesia. Always follow your own team's instructions.

habits.title: Ask if you are at risk of poor nutrition
habits.why: People who are poorly nourished may be given nutrition drinks before major surgery.

doctorQuestions: Which of my supplements should I stop, and exactly when?
Should I keep taking my usual medicines, such as blood thinners, metformin or weight-loss injections, up to surgery?
Should I have a blood test for anaemia or low iron before surgery?
When can I restart my supplements afterwards?
What can I eat and drink before the operation?

conditions.name: Recent surgery (recovering)
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you had an operation in the last few weeks? What kind, and are you still healing?

flags.why: Not eating enough after major surgery raises the risk of problems. Ask your team how much food and protein you need.
High-dose vitamin C did not speed up healing of pressure sores in a trial.
Low zinc can slow wound healing in older adults. Taking 50 mg or more a day for weeks can lower copper.
If you have iron-deficiency anaemia, guidelines advise iron after surgery too.
One small trial found collagen helped pressure sores shrink. This evidence is from pressure sores, not surgical wounds.

flags.nutrient: garlic, ginkgo, ginseng and high-dose vitamin E
flags.why: These can increase bleeding. Ask before restarting while wounds heal.

habits.title: Eat and drink as soon as your team allows
habits.why: Starting to eat within hours of most operations is advised.

habits.title: Get up and move as early as your team advises
habits.why: Early movement helps the body use protein and keeps muscles working.

habits.title: Learn the signs of a blood clot
habits.why: Pain and swelling in one leg needs an urgent check. Chest pain or breathlessness needs emergency help.

doctorQuestions: Which supplements can I restart, and when?
Should I take extra protein or a nutrition drink while I recover?
Do I need a blood test for iron or anaemia?
What warning signs in my wound or legs should I watch for?

conditions.name: Thyroid condition
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you have a thyroid condition, such as an underactive or overactive thyroid, Hashimoto's or Graves' disease? Do you take thyroid tablets such as levothyroxine?

flags.why: Calcium can block levothyroxine. Take them at least 4 hours apart.
Iron can block levothyroxine. Take them at least 4 hours apart.
High-dose biotin can make thyroid blood tests look falsely high or low. Tell your doctor before a test.
People with autoimmune thyroid disease may get side effects even at iodine amounts that are safe for others. Seaweed products vary a lot in iodine.
Trial results in autoimmune thyroid disease are mixed. Do not go above 400 mcg a day.
Experts do not recommend it for people with thyroid disorders, and it might interact with thyroid hormone medicine.
Listed as not mixing well with levothyroxine.
A small study found it reduced levothyroxine absorption. Ask a pharmacist how to space them.
Foods with soy, walnuts and dietary fibre may affect how levothyroxine works. Keep your routine the same each day.

habits.title: Take levothyroxine on an empty stomach, 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast, coffee or other medicines
habits.why: Some foods can affect how it works.

habits.title: Keep calcium and iron supplements at least 4 hours away from levothyroxine
habits.why: These minerals can stop the tablet being absorbed.

doctorQuestions: Is my levothyroxine dose right, and when should my thyroid be rechecked?
Should I pause biotin before my next thyroid blood test?
Are iodine, selenium or herbal products safe for my thyroid condition?
How should I time my other supplements around my thyroid tablet?

conditions.name: Haemochromatosis (iron overload)
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you been told you have haemochromatosis or too much iron in your body?

flags.why: Do not take iron supplements; they may be harmful when iron is already high.
High doses of vitamin C could make iron overload worse.

flags.nutrient: multivitamins with iron or vitamin C
flags.why: Treatment includes avoiding iron and vitamin C supplements, so check multivitamin labels.
Avoid cereals with added iron.

habits.title: Keep alcohol low
habits.why: Alcohol can increase iron in the body and strain the liver.

habits.title: Do not eat raw oysters or clams
habits.why: They can carry bacteria that cause serious infections in people with high iron.

doctorQuestions: How often do I need venesection (blood removal), and what are my iron targets?
Is my liver healthy?
Which supplements and multivitamins are safe for me?

conditions.name: Low iron or iron-deficiency anaemia
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you been told your iron is low or that you have iron-deficiency anaemia? Are you taking iron tablets?

flags.why: Take iron tablets as your doctor advises, usually for about 6 months, with repeat blood tests to check progress.
In a small trial in women with low iron, one morning dose on alternate days was absorbed better than daily or split doses. Ask your doctor before changing how you take it.
Calcium may get in the way of iron absorption. Take calcium and iron supplements at different times.
High zinc doses over weeks can lower copper. Stay within 40 mg a day.
Low iron increases manganese absorption and can make manganese toxicity worse.

habits.title: Take iron with or soon after food if it upsets your stomach
habits.why: This can reduce side effects such as feeling sick and constipation.

habits.title: Drink a glass of orange juice after your iron tablet
habits.why: This may help your body absorb the iron.

habits.title: Avoid tea, coffee and milk around the time you take iron
habits.why: These can stop your body absorbing iron.

habits.title: Eat iron-rich foods such as meat, beans, lentils, dark green vegetables and fortified cereals
habits.why: Your GP may advise more iron-rich foods if diet is part of the cause.

doctorQuestions: What is causing my low iron, and do I need more tests?
How long should I take iron, and when will you recheck my blood?
Should I take iron every day or every other day?
What should I do if the tablets upset my stomach?

conditions.name: Low vitamin B12
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you been told your vitamin B12 is low, or do you have B12 injections or tablets?

flags.why: Follow your doctor's plan. Some people need injections for life, others tablets, depending on the cause.
Large amounts of folic acid can correct the anaemia of B12 deficiency but not the nerve damage, so the problem can be missed. Stay within 1,000 mcg a day unless your doctor advises more.

habits.title: Eat B12 foods or fortified foods if your diet is low in animal foods
habits.why: Fortified cereals, yeast extracts and soy products can help.

doctorQuestions: What is causing my low B12?
Do I need injections or tablets, and for how long?
Could any of my medicines, such as metformin or stomach acid tablets, be a cause?

conditions.name: Low vitamin D
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you been told your vitamin D is low, or are you rarely outdoors in daylight?

flags.why: Adults need 10 mcg (400 IU) a day. Take it all year if you are rarely outdoors, live in a care home or cover most of your skin; consider it all year if you have dark skin.
Do not take more than 100 mcg (4,000 IU) a day unless your doctor advises it. Too much over a long time can raise calcium and damage the kidneys and heart.

habits.title: Get some daylight on your skin from late March to September
habits.why: Most people make enough vitamin D from summer sun.

doctorQuestions: What dose of vitamin D do I need, and for how long?
Do I need a repeat blood test?
Are any of my medicines affecting my vitamin D?

conditions.name: Osteoporosis or weak bones
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you been told you have osteoporosis or thin bones, or had a broken bone from a minor fall?

flags.why: Calcium supplements are absorbed best in doses of 500 mg or less. Bone tablets like alendronic acid must be taken apart from calcium.
Consider 10 mcg (400 IU) a day. Your doctor may advise more if you are low.
More than 1,500 mcg vitamin A a day over many years may make bones more likely to break.
Magnesium supplements or antacids can stop bone tablets such as alendronate being absorbed. Take them at least 2 hours apart.

habits.title: Do weight-bearing and strength exercise
habits.why: These help bone strength. Check with your doctor first if you have osteoporosis.

habits.title: Do strength and balance exercises to prevent falls
habits.why: US experts recommend exercise to prevent falls in adults 65 and over at higher risk.

doctorQuestions: Do I need bone medicine, and how should I take it?
Should I take calcium or vitamin D, and how much?
Is my exercise plan safe for my bones?

conditions.name: Vegan or vegetarian diet
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you follow a vegan or vegetarian diet, or eat little or no meat, fish, eggs or dairy?

flags.why: B12 comes naturally only from animal foods. Vegans need fortified foods or a supplement.
Vegans may not get enough iodine. Use fortified foods or a supplement, but avoid kelp and seaweed products.
People on vegetarian diets need about 1.8 times more iron.
Plant foods contain phytates that reduce zinc absorption.
Use calcium-fortified dairy alternatives or other good plant sources.
Consider a daily vitamin D supplement, at least in autumn and winter.
Selenium can be harder to get on a vegan diet.
Vegans who consume little milk may be low in riboflavin.
Eat omega-3 rich nuts and seeds, such as walnuts, every day.

habits.title: Plan meals with fortified dairy alternatives, beans, pulses, nuts and seeds
habits.why: With good planning, a vegan diet can give the nutrients you need.

habits.title: Eat vitamin C foods with plant iron sources
habits.why: Vitamin C helps the body absorb iron from plant foods.

doctorQuestions: Should my B12, iron or vitamin D be checked?
Which fortified foods or supplements do I need?
If I am pregnant or breastfeeding, what extra does my baby need?

conditions.name: Aged 65 or over
conditions.intakeQuestion: Are you aged 65 or over?

flags.why: About 8 to 9% of adults aged 65 and over have a stomach condition that lowers B12 absorption. Ask about a B12 test, especially if you take metformin or stomach acid tablets.
Consider 10 mcg (400 IU) a day in autumn and winter, or all year if you are frail, housebound or rarely outdoors.
In a large trial, vitamin D did not lower fractures in healthy older adults who were not low.
US experts advise against low-dose calcium with vitamin D to prevent fractures in women after menopause who live at home.
Over many years, more than 1,500 mcg a day of vitamin A may make bones more likely to break. Check multivitamins and fish liver oils.
Older adults need more protein than younger adults, about 1.0 to 1.2 g per kg of body weight a day, unless they have severe kidney disease.
Older adults are more likely to be low, but the risk of too much magnesium rises if kidneys are weak.
Salt substitutes with potassium are not advised for older people.

habits.title: Do strength, balance and flexibility exercises at least 2 days a week
habits.why: US experts recommend exercise to prevent falls in adults 65 and over at higher risk of falling.

habits.title: Aim for 150 minutes of moderate activity a week and be active every day
habits.why: This is the national advice for adults aged 65 and over.

habits.title: Eat enough protein and stay active together
habits.why: Experts advise both to help older people keep muscle and function.

doctorQuestions: Should my B12, vitamin D or kidney function be checked?
Are all my medicines and supplements still needed and safe together?
Am I at risk of falls or weak bones, and would a bone scan help?

conditions.name: Smoking
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you smoke or use tobacco?

flags.why: In two large trials, beta-carotene supplements increased lung cancer risk in smokers.
Smokers need 35 mg more vitamin C a day. Food is the best source.
In a trial of male smokers, vitamin E was linked to more bleeding strokes.

habits.title: Get support to stop smoking
habits.why: Free stop smoking services and tools can help you quit.

doctorQuestions: What stop-smoking support or medicine could help me?
Should my lungs or heart be checked?

conditions.name: Gout
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you had gout, or been told your uric acid is high?

flags.why: Doctors stop high-dose niacin if acute gout develops.

flags.nutrient: diets or supplements sold for gout
flags.why: UK guidance says there is not enough evidence that any specific diet prevents gout flares or lowers uric acid.

habits.title: Keep to a healthy weight and avoid heavy drinking
habits.why: Excess weight and alcohol may make gout flares worse.

habits.title: Drink enough fluids
habits.why: Being dehydrated can trigger a gout attack.

doctorQuestions: Do I need medicine to lower my uric acid?
Are any of my medicines making gout worse?

conditions.name: Inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis)
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you have Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis?

flags.why: Some bowel operations, such as removing the end of the small bowel, are a common risk factor for low B12.
Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis can reduce vitamin D absorption.
Conditions such as ulcerative colitis can reduce iron absorption.
15 to 40% of people with inflammatory bowel disease have low zinc.
Crohn's disease and bowel surgery can lower magnesium.
Probiotics can rarely cause serious infections in people with weak immune systems, for example on strong immune-suppressing medicines.

habits.title: Ask for diet and nutrition advice
habits.why: UK guidance says people with Crohn's disease should be given information on diet and nutrition.

doctorQuestions: Should my iron, B12, vitamin D and zinc be checked?
Are supplements safe with my immune-suppressing medicines?
Do I need a dietitian?

conditions.name: Coeliac disease
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you have coeliac disease?

flags.why: Coeliac disease can cause low iron. A GP or dietitian may advise supplements if needed.
Coeliac disease is a common risk factor for low B12.
Coeliac disease can cause low folate.
Coeliac disease can reduce vitamin D absorption.
Coeliac disease can be linked to weak bones; your doctor may check whether you need a bone scan.
In one study, 15% of people with coeliac disease had low copper.

habits.title: Follow a strict gluten-free diet, with help from a dietitian
habits.why: This is the main treatment. Symptoms usually improve within weeks.

doctorQuestions: Do I need blood tests for iron, B12, folate or vitamin D?
Do I need a bone density scan?
Can I see a dietitian?

conditions.name: Weight-loss surgery
conditions.intakeQuestion: Have you had weight-loss surgery, such as a gastric bypass or sleeve gastrectomy?

flags.why: Many weight-loss operations reduce B12 absorption.
Severe thiamin deficiency can happen after weight-loss surgery and can damage the brain and nerves.
Gastric bypass reduces vitamin D absorption.
After weight-loss surgery, nutrition needs special attention from your care team.
Zinc can be poorly absorbed, or lost in urine, after weight-loss surgery.
If you are planning a pregnancy, ask your surgery team for advice on folic acid and other nutrients.

habits.title: Take the supplements your surgery team prescribes, and keep up follow-up checks
habits.why: Guidelines stress special attention to nutrition after weight-loss surgery.

doctorQuestions: Which supplements do I need for life, and at what doses?
How often should my blood levels be checked?
What signs of low vitamins should I watch for?

conditions.name: Having cancer treatment
conditions.intakeQuestion: Are you having treatment for cancer now, such as chemotherapy, radiotherapy, hormone therapy or targeted drugs?

flags.why: Ask your cancer team before taking vitamin C or other antioxidants, especially in high doses, during chemotherapy or radiotherapy.
Cancer doctors often advise against antioxidant supplements during chemotherapy or radiotherapy, because they might make treatment work less well.
It can weaken some cancer medicines.
Talk to your cancer team first. Curcumin may interact with some chemotherapy medicines.
If you take methotrexate for cancer, ask your cancer doctor before taking folic acid, as it could interfere with treatment.
CoQ10 may not be compatible with some types of cancer treatment.
In people with weak immune systems, probiotics have rarely caused serious blood infections.
Cisplatin, a chemotherapy medicine, can lower selenium, but it is not clear whether this matters or whether supplements help.

habits.title: Show your cancer team every supplement before you start it
habits.why: Some supplements, especially antioxidants, may change how cancer treatments work.

doctorQuestions: Which of my supplements are safe during my treatment?
Should I stop any supplements before or after each treatment?
Do I need help from a dietitian to eat enough?

conditions.name: Weakened immune system
conditions.intakeQuestion: Is your immune system weakened by a condition or medicine, for example an organ transplant, chemotherapy, HIV, or strong steroid or immune-suppressing medicines?

flags.why: Probiotics have been linked to serious blood infections, mainly in people who are very ill or have weak immune systems.
It can weaken ciclosporin, a transplant medicine, and some HIV and cancer medicines.
In kidney transplant patients it raised blood levels of ciclosporin.
Tell your doctor before taking turmeric if you take tacrolimus, a transplant medicine.
It might interact with medicines that suppress the immune system.
After a kidney transplant, some herb interactions can make anti-rejection medicines work less well.

habits.title: Bring your supplement bottles, or a photo of the labels, to appointments
habits.why: Your care team can look up each ingredient for safety.

doctorQuestions: Which supplements are safe with my medicines?
Are probiotics safe for me?
Do I need any vitamin levels checked?

conditions.name: Epilepsy
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you have epilepsy or take medicine to prevent seizures?

flags.why: Some seizure medicines lower folate, and folate supplements might lower the medicine level. Check with your doctor before taking it.
If you are planning a pregnancy or in early pregnancy, UK guidelines advise a higher prescribed dose (5 mg a day) for people taking anti-epileptic medicines.
High doses (200 mg a day) may lower blood levels of phenytoin and phenobarbital.
It can weaken seizure medicines such as phenytoin and carbamazepine.
It might interact with seizure medicines.
CBD is listed as possibly interacting with valproate.

flags.nutrient: antacids with calcium, magnesium or aluminium
flags.why: These are listed as possibly interacting with phenytoin.
Vitamin D is listed as possibly interacting with phenytoin. Ask your doctor about the right amount.
Taking seizure medicine for at least a year is linked to lower biotin levels.

habits.title: Take your seizure medicine every day and do not change it without advice
habits.why: Missing doses or changing treatment can lead to seizures.

habits.title: Do not drink too much alcohol
habits.why: Too much alcohol can increase the risk of seizures.

doctorQuestions: Are my supplements safe with my seizure medicine?
Do I need folic acid, and at what dose?
Should my vitamin D or bone health be checked?

conditions.name: Migraine
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you get migraines?

flags.why: Magnesium is probably effective for preventing migraines, with modest benefit in trials. Trial doses (up to 600 mg) are above the 350 mg upper limit, so ask your doctor first.
Riboflavin is probably effective for preventing migraines. 400 mg a day cut attacks by about two a month in one trial.

flags.nutrient: caffeine (including energy drinks and pre-workout products)
flags.why: Too much caffeine can trigger migraine attacks.

habits.title: Keep a migraine diary
habits.why: It can help you find your triggers.

habits.title: Eat at regular times, sleep well and stay hydrated
habits.why: Skipping meals, tiredness and stress are common triggers.

habits.title: Exercise regularly and limit alcohol and caffeine
habits.why: These are advised to help manage migraine.

doctorQuestions: Should I try a preventive treatment?
Are magnesium or vitamin B2 suitable for me?
Could any of my medicines be making headaches worse?

conditions.name: Menopause or perimenopause
conditions.intakeQuestion: Are you going through the menopause or perimenopause, or have you been through it?

flags.why: There is some evidence it may ease hot flushes, but products vary, safety is uncertain and interactions have been reported.
Rare cases of liver damage have been reported. See a doctor if you get dark urine or tiredness.
There is some evidence they may ease hot flushes, but products vary and safety is uncertain.
If you have had breast cancer, it may interact with tamoxifen, blood thinners and seizure medicines.
Eat calcium-rich foods such as milk, yoghurt and kale to protect your bones.
Vitamin D helps keep bones healthy. Taking a supplement is advised.

habits.title: Do weight-bearing and resistance exercise
habits.why: Helps keep bones healthy after the menopause.

habits.title: Cut down on hot flush triggers like spicy food, caffeine, smoking and alcohol
habits.why: These can trigger hot flushes.

doctorQuestions: Is HRT an option for me?
Are herbal remedies safe with my medicines?
Should my bone health be checked?

conditions.name: Heavy periods
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you have heavy periods, for example needing to change pads or tampons very often, or bleeding through to clothes?

flags.why: Heavy periods are a common cause of low iron. Guidelines advise a full blood count for everyone with heavy periods.
Heavy periods may cause about a third of iron-deficiency anaemia in women.

habits.title: See a GP if heavy periods stop you doing daily activities, or you often feel tired or short of breath
habits.why: These can be signs of low iron or another cause that needs checking.

doctorQuestions: Should my blood count and iron be checked?
What could be causing my heavy periods?
What treatments could make my periods lighter?

conditions.name: Regular or heavy drinking
conditions.intakeQuestion: How many alcoholic drinks do you usually have in a week, and do you sometimes drink a lot in one go?

flags.why: Up to 80% of people with long-term heavy drinking develop low thiamin, which can damage the brain. Ask your doctor about thiamin.
Alcohol reduces how well the body absorbs and uses folate.
Alcohol dependence can lower magnesium.
30 to 50% of people with alcohol use disorder have low zinc.
B6 levels tend to be very low in people who depend on alcohol.
Do not combine kava with alcohol. Kava has been linked to rare, serious liver injury.
Valerian should not be taken with alcohol or sedatives.

habits.title: Keep to no more than 14 units a week, spread over 3 or more days
habits.why: This is the UK low-risk drinking advice for adults.

habits.title: Have several drink-free days each week
habits.why: This helps if you want to cut down.

doctorQuestions: Would thiamin or other vitamins help me?
Should my liver be checked?
Are my medicines safe with alcohol?

conditions.name: Training hard or competing in sport
conditions.intakeQuestion: Do you train hard or compete in sport most weeks?

flags.why: Athletes may need 1.2 to 2.0 g of protein per kg of body weight a day; up to about 2.0 g/kg is considered safe.
Protein supplements and high muscle mass can make a common kidney blood test less reliable. Tell your doctor if you take them.
May help strength and power in short, hard efforts, but often causes water weight gain. Few safety concerns at usual doses.
Kidney experts list creatine as high risk if you have kidney disease.
Up to 400 mg a day is not usually dangerous for healthy adults. Too much can cause a fast or irregular heartbeat and poor sleep.
Athletes can lose extra iron through sweat and foot impact. Correcting iron-deficiency anaemia improves work capacity.
Ingredient amounts vary widely between products, and makers rarely fund good research on them.
Vegetarian athletes are at higher risk of low riboflavin.

habits.title: Aim for 1.2 to 2.0 g protein per kg of body weight a day
habits.why: This range is suggested for athletes and is considered safe for healthy people.

doctorQuestions: Do I need my iron checked?
Is creatine or caffeine safe for me?
Are my sports supplements safe with my health and medicines?

medications.name: Metformin

interactions.effect: Long-term use can lower B12, more so at higher doses and over longer time. This can cause tiredness, a sore red tongue, pins and needles or anaemia.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor about a B12 blood test now and then, and straight away if these symptoms appear. Do not stop metformin on your own.

interactions.effect: In a study it lowered metformin levels by about a quarter, which could weaken blood sugar control.
interactions.action: Avoid unless your doctor agrees.

interactions.effect: May add to the sugar-lowering effect, and it can change how the body handles some medicines.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor before using it with metformin.

interactions.effect: May add to the sugar-lowering effect.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor first; check your sugar more often.

interactions.effect: Drinking alcohol raises the risk of a serious side effect called lactic acidosis and may lower blood sugar.
interactions.action: Limit alcohol and ask your doctor how much is safe.

medications.name: Insulin and sulfonylureas (for example insulin, gliclazide, glimepiride, glipizide)

interactions.effect: May increase insulin sensitivity and raise the risk of low blood sugar.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor first and check your sugar more often.

interactions.effect: May add to the sugar-lowering effect of these medicines, so blood sugar could drop too low.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor before using it.

interactions.effect: Large doses may cause a harmful drop in blood sugar.
interactions.action: Avoid supplement doses unless your doctor agrees.

interactions.effect: Large doses of niacin can raise blood sugar.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor before high-dose niacin; your sugar may need closer checks.

interactions.effect: CoQ10 may interact with insulin.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor first.

interactions.effect: Alcohol can cause low blood sugar, sometimes hours later.
interactions.action: Check your sugar after drinking and ask your doctor what is safe.

medications.name: Warfarin

interactions.effect: Changes in vitamin K intake can make warfarin work more or less.
interactions.action: Do not take vitamin K supplements. Keep vitamin K foods steady week to week.

interactions.effect: It can weaken warfarin, so clots are more likely.
interactions.action: Do not take it with warfarin.

interactions.effect: Can increase bleeding risk with warfarin, especially at high doses.
interactions.action: Avoid high-dose vitamin E unless your doctor agrees.

interactions.effect: May increase bleeding risk.
interactions.action: Avoid unless your doctor agrees.

interactions.effect: Garlic supplements may increase bleeding.
interactions.action: Avoid supplement doses; food amounts are fine.

interactions.effect: Listed as interacting with warfarin.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor first.

interactions.effect: Listed as interacting with warfarin and may affect clotting.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor first.

interactions.effect: Fish oil at 3 to 6 g a day usually does not change warfarin much, but INR should be checked from time to time.
interactions.action: Tell your anticoagulation clinic before starting.

interactions.effect: May increase bleeding risk with warfarin and other blood thinners.
interactions.action: Avoid supplement doses unless your doctor agrees.

interactions.effect: Listed as possibly interacting with warfarin.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor first.

interactions.effect: UK advice is to avoid them while taking warfarin.
interactions.action: Do not have cranberry juice or cranberry products.

medications.name: DOACs, blood thinners (for example apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, edoxaban)

interactions.effect: Listed as not mixing well with apixaban and rivaroxaban.
interactions.action: Do not take St John's wort without asking your doctor.

interactions.effect: With dabigatran it is expected to lower drug levels, and taking them together should be avoided.
interactions.action: Do not take it with dabigatran.

interactions.effect: May increase bleeding risk with blood thinners.
interactions.action: Avoid unless your doctor agrees.

interactions.effect: Garlic supplements may increase bleeding.
interactions.action: Avoid supplement doses.

interactions.effect: May increase bleeding risk with blood thinners.
interactions.action: Avoid supplement doses unless your doctor agrees.

interactions.effect: Can reduce platelet clumping and may raise bleeding risk with blood thinners.
interactions.action: Avoid high doses unless your doctor agrees.

interactions.nutrient: all vitamins, supplements and herbal products
interactions.effect: Your doctor may need to change doses or watch you closely for side effects.
interactions.action: Tell your doctor or pharmacist about every supplement.

medications.name: Antiplatelet medicines (for example aspirin, clopidogrel)

interactions.effect: With clopidogrel it can raise drug levels and bleeding risk.
interactions.action: Do not take it with clopidogrel unless your doctor agrees.

interactions.effect: Herbs that affect the blood, such as ginkgo, may cause problems with clopidogrel.
interactions.action: Avoid unless your doctor agrees.

interactions.effect: Garlic supplements may increase bleeding, especially with aspirin.
interactions.action: Avoid supplement doses.

interactions.effect: Can reduce platelet clumping and may add to bleeding risk.
interactions.action: Avoid high doses unless your doctor agrees.

interactions.effect: High-dose fish oil can have a mild antiplatelet effect, less strong than aspirin.
interactions.action: Tell your doctor if you take high doses.

interactions.effect: Products containing aesculin may add to bleeding risk with aspirin or other blood thinners.
interactions.action: Avoid unless your doctor agrees.

medications.name: Levothyroxine (thyroid hormone)

interactions.effect: Calcium carbonate can stop levothyroxine being absorbed.
interactions.action: Take them at least 4 hours apart.

interactions.effect: Taking iron at the same time can clearly reduce how well levothyroxine works.
interactions.action: Take them at least 4 hours apart.

interactions.effect: Biotin can affect thyroid blood test results.
interactions.action: Tell your doctor before blood tests.

interactions.effect: Listed as not mixing well with levothyroxine.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor first.

interactions.effect: A small study found chromium reduced levothyroxine absorption.
interactions.action: Ask your pharmacist how to space them.

interactions.effect: Antacids and other indigestion treatments are listed as not mixing well with levothyroxine.
interactions.action: Take at a different time; ask your pharmacist.

interactions.effect: Foods with soy, walnuts and dietary fibre may affect how levothyroxine works.
interactions.action: Keep your routine the same each day.

interactions.effect: May raise thyroid hormone levels and might interact with thyroid medicines.
interactions.action: Avoid unless your doctor agrees.

medications.name: Statins (for example atorvastatin, simvastatin, rosuvastatin)

interactions.effect: Some products contain a statin-like drug, with the same possible side effects (muscle, kidney and liver damage) and interactions.
interactions.action: Do not take it with a statin unless your doctor agrees.

interactions.effect: Can weaken some statins, such as simvastatin.
interactions.action: Avoid unless your doctor agrees.

interactions.effect: Added to a statin in large trials, high-dose niacin did not lower heart events and caused more side effects.
interactions.action: Do not add high-dose niacin unless a specialist advises it.

interactions.effect: Statins might not work as well with high-dose vitamin D.
interactions.action: Keep vitamin D within usual amounts unless your doctor advises more.

interactions.effect: Can lower blood levels of atorvastatin.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor before using it.

interactions.effect: Too much grapefruit juice can raise the chance of side effects with atorvastatin.
interactions.action: Have no more than 1 or 2 small glasses a day, and check your own statin leaflet.

interactions.effect: Research does not show that CoQ10 reduces muscle pain caused by statins.
interactions.action: Talk to your doctor about muscle pain.

medications.name: Stomach acid reducers: PPIs and H2 blockers (for example omeprazole, lansoprazole, famotidine)

interactions.effect: These medicines can reduce B12 absorption from food.
interactions.action: Ask about a B12 test if you take them long term.

interactions.effect: Long-term PPI use (usually over a year) can cause low magnesium.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor about a magnesium blood test.

interactions.effect: These medicines reduce iron absorption; iron tablets may work less well.
interactions.action: Tell your doctor if you are being treated for low iron.

interactions.effect: Calcium carbonate is absorbed less well with low stomach acid unless taken with a meal.
interactions.action: Take calcium carbonate with food, or ask about calcium citrate.

interactions.effect: May stop lansoprazole working as well as it should, and is listed as not mixing well with omeprazole.
interactions.action: Do not take it with these medicines.

medications.name: Antacids (for example calcium carbonate, magnesium or aluminium indigestion remedies)

interactions.effect: Calcium-based antacids may get in the way of iron absorption.
interactions.action: Take iron and calcium products at different times.

interactions.effect: Calcium carbonate can affect other medicines taken at the same time.
interactions.action: Do not take calcium carbonate within 1 to 2 hours of other medicines.

interactions.effect: Calcium-based antacids add to your daily calcium. The upper limit is 2,500 mg a day up to age 50 and 2,000 mg a day after that.
interactions.action: Count antacids in your daily calcium total.

interactions.effect: Magnesium in antacids counts toward the 350 mg a day upper limit from supplements and medicines. Too much is more likely if kidneys are weak.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor if you have kidney disease.

interactions.effect: Antacids reduce chromium absorption.
interactions.action: Take them at different times.

medications.name: Tetracycline and quinolone antibiotics (for example doxycycline, ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin)

interactions.effect: Calcium binds these antibiotics so less is absorbed.
interactions.action: Take calcium products at least 6 hours before or 2 hours after ciprofloxacin. Timings differ by antibiotic, so check with your pharmacist.

interactions.effect: Iron binds these antibiotics so less is absorbed.
interactions.action: Take iron 3 hours before or 2 hours after doxycycline. Check timing for other antibiotics with your pharmacist.

interactions.effect: Zinc binds these antibiotics.
interactions.action: Take the antibiotic at least 2 hours before or 4 to 6 hours after zinc.

interactions.effect: Magnesium binds these antibiotics.
interactions.action: Take the antibiotic at least 2 hours before or 4 to 6 hours after magnesium.

interactions.effect: Minerals in multivitamins can reduce antibiotic absorption.
interactions.action: Space them as for the single minerals; ask your pharmacist.

medications.name: ACE inhibitors and ARBs (for example ramipril, lisinopril, losartan, candesartan)

interactions.effect: These medicines reduce potassium loss in urine and can cause high potassium.
interactions.action: Do not take potassium supplements unless your doctor prescribes them.

interactions.effect: Salt substitutes that contain potassium can raise potassium.
interactions.action: Do not use them without talking to your doctor.

interactions.effect: Potassium iodide with ACE inhibitors can raise the risk of high potassium.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor before taking potassium iodide.

interactions.effect: Even small amounts of licorice root products have been linked to severe side effects in people with high blood pressure.
interactions.action: Avoid licorice supplements.

interactions.effect: Might interact with blood pressure medicines.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor first.

medications.name: Potassium-sparing water tablets (for example spironolactone, eplerenone, amiloride)

interactions.effect: These medicines can raise potassium, and potassium supplements may not mix well with them.
interactions.action: Do not take potassium supplements unless your doctor prescribes them.

interactions.effect: Potassium salt substitutes can raise potassium levels further.
interactions.action: Avoid them; ask a doctor or dietitian.

interactions.effect: These medicines reduce magnesium loss in urine.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor before magnesium supplements.

interactions.effect: Potassium iodide can raise potassium with these medicines.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor first.

medications.name: Thiazide water tablets (for example bendroflumethiazide, indapamide, hydrochlorothiazide)

interactions.effect: With vitamin D supplements, blood calcium could rise too high.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor before vitamin D above usual amounts.

interactions.effect: Calcium supplements are listed as not mixing well with indapamide.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor before calcium supplements.

interactions.effect: These medicines increase zinc loss in urine.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor if a zinc check is needed.

interactions.effect: These medicines increase magnesium loss in urine.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor about magnesium checks.

interactions.effect: These medicines increase potassium loss in urine and can cause low potassium.
interactions.action: Only take potassium if your doctor advises it.

interactions.effect: Licorice can cause serious side effects, especially in people with high blood pressure.
interactions.action: Avoid licorice supplements.

medications.name: Loop water tablets (for example furosemide, bumetanide)

interactions.effect: Supplements that raise potassium may not mix well with furosemide.
interactions.action: Only take potassium if your doctor advises it and checks your blood.

interactions.effect: These medicines increase magnesium loss in urine.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor about magnesium checks.

interactions.effect: Furosemide can lower thiamin levels through urine.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor whether thiamin is needed.

interactions.effect: Licorice can cause serious heart rhythm problems.
interactions.action: Avoid licorice supplements.

medications.name: Bone medicines: bisphosphonates (for example alendronic acid, risedronate)

interactions.effect: The bone tablet works best on an empty stomach, so calcium and food at the same time get in the way.
interactions.action: Take the bone tablet first with plain tap water; wait at least 30 minutes before calcium, food or other medicines.

interactions.effect: Magnesium supplements and antacids reduce absorption of these bone medicines.
interactions.action: Keep magnesium at least 2 hours away.

interactions.effect: Supplements with iron are listed as something to tell your doctor about.
interactions.action: Tell your doctor; take iron at a different time of day.

interactions.effect: Supplements with zinc are listed as something to tell your doctor about.
interactions.action: Tell your doctor; take zinc at a different time of day.

interactions.effect: Vitamins, supplements and antacids taken at the same time can stop the medicine working.
interactions.action: Take them at least 30 minutes after the bone tablet.

medications.name: SSRI and SNRI antidepressants (for example sertraline, citalopram, fluoxetine, venlafaxine)

interactions.effect: With some antidepressants it can cause serotonin-related side effects, which can be serious.
interactions.action: Do not take St John's wort with these medicines.

interactions.effect: Raises serotonin. With these medicines there is a possible risk of serotonin syndrome, a serious reaction.
interactions.action: Do not take 5-HTP unless your doctor supervises it.

interactions.effect: Listed as possibly interacting with sertraline, fluoxetine and venlafaxine.
interactions.action: Do not take tryptophan unless your doctor agrees.

interactions.effect: National medicine advice says not to use it with sertraline, citalopram, fluoxetine or venlafaxine.
interactions.action: Avoid it completely while on these medicines.

medications.name: Hormonal contraceptive pills (for example the combined pill)

interactions.effect: Can weaken birth control pills, so pregnancy could happen.
interactions.action: Do not take it with the pill without advice; ask about other contraception.

interactions.effect: The combined pill can lower B12 blood test results without a real deficiency.
interactions.action: Tell your doctor you take the pill if your B12 is tested.

medications.name: Steroid tablets (for example prednisolone, prednisone)

interactions.effect: Steroids such as prednisone can lower vitamin D levels.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor if you need vitamin D, especially on long courses.

interactions.effect: Your doctor may advise a high-calcium diet or a calcium supplement.
interactions.action: Follow your doctor's advice on calcium.

interactions.effect: Your doctor may advise a high-potassium diet or a supplement.
interactions.action: Only take potassium if your doctor advises it.

interactions.effect: Listed as possibly interacting with prednisone.
interactions.action: Avoid unless your doctor agrees.

interactions.effect: Interactions between licorice and corticosteroids have been reported.
interactions.action: Avoid licorice supplements.

medications.name: Methotrexate

interactions.effect: Your doctor may prescribe folic acid with methotrexate. Do not take extra folic acid or folate from other products on top.
interactions.action: Do not take folic acid or folate-containing vitamins unless your doctor says so.

interactions.effect: If you take methotrexate for cancer, folate supplements could interfere with how it works.
interactions.action: Ask your cancer doctor before any folate supplement.

interactions.effect: Heavy drinking and liver disease matter with methotrexate.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor about the safe use of alcohol.

medications.name: Anti-seizure medicines (for example carbamazepine, phenytoin, sodium valproate, lamotrigine)

interactions.effect: Some of these medicines lower folate, and folate supplements might lower the medicine level.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor before folic acid. If you are planning a pregnancy, a higher prescribed dose may be advised.

interactions.effect: Can weaken phenytoin and carbamazepine.
interactions.action: Do not take it with these medicines.

interactions.effect: High doses (200 mg a day) may lower phenytoin and phenobarbital levels.
interactions.action: Avoid high-dose B6 unless your doctor agrees.

interactions.effect: Listed as possibly interacting with phenytoin.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor about vitamin D.

interactions.effect: Antacids with calcium, magnesium or aluminium are listed as possibly interacting with phenytoin.
interactions.action: Ask your pharmacist how to space them.

interactions.effect: Using these medicines for a year or more is linked to lower biotin levels.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor if this matters for you.

interactions.effect: Listed as possibly interacting with valproate.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor first.

interactions.effect: Might interact with anti-seizure medicines.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor first.

medications.name: Lithium

interactions.effect: Long-term lithium can raise blood calcium, and calcium supplements could add to this.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor before calcium supplements.

interactions.effect: Listed as possibly interacting with lithium.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor first.

interactions.effect: There is not enough information to say they are safe with lithium.
interactions.action: Ask your doctor or pharmacist before any supplement.

interactions.effect: Your doctor may want to know how much tea, coffee or cola you drink.
interactions.action: Talk to your doctor about caffeine drinks.

interactions.effect: It is important to get the right amounts of fluid and salt while taking lithium.
interactions.action: Follow your doctor's advice on salt and fluids.

pauseBeforeSurgery.supplement: all herbal and dietary supplements (default if no specific advice)
pauseBeforeSurgery.why: Anaesthetists may ask you to stop supplements at least 2 weeks before. This is caution, not proof of harm. Always follow your own surgical team.
Garlic supplements may increase bleeding. A 2001 review advised stopping at least 7 days before; some teams ask for 2 weeks.
A 2001 review advised stopping at least 36 hours before surgery because of possible bleeding. Some teams ask for 2 weeks.
May increase bleeding and lower blood sugar. A 2001 review advised stopping at least 7 days before.
Speeds up how the body clears many medicines used around surgery. A 2001 review advised stopping at least 5 days before.
May make anaesthetic drugs stronger. A 2001 review advised stopping at least 24 hours before; some teams ask for 2 weeks.
May prolong anaesthesia. If possible taper it over the weeks before surgery; if not, a review advised continuing until surgery. Do not stop suddenly after long use.
Often stopped before surgery because of a possible bleeding risk, but the evidence is weak: a small study found 800 IU a day for 2 weeks did not change bleeding time or platelet function.
Evidence does not support stopping. In a large heart-surgery trial (OPERA), high-dose fish oil did not increase bleeding and fewer blood transfusions were needed. Follow your team's advice.
Listed in guidance based on a 2021 expert consensus among supplements to hold 2 weeks before surgery, because of a theoretical bleeding risk.

A 2001 review advised stopping as far ahead as possible, especially for people with liver problems or a transplant. 14 days is a practical default.
Experts do not recommend ashwagandha for people about to have surgery. No exact stop time is given, so use the usual 2-week default unless told otherwise.
